pageCache.text:
We strive to work closely and in partnership with parents and the community to provide a safe, caring and inspiring environment where children are supported, challenged and encouraged to be the best they can be.
Our next Open Morning is on Saturday 14th November 10am -12pm. Come and chat to staff and governors.
Headteacher's Welcome
At its centre, Woodchester is a school that exudes inclusivity and welcome. It is, and always has been, a caring school.
It is a privilege to be entrusted with guiding children through their primary school years. These are precious and important years, when children grow, change and develop in so many ways. At Woodchester, we want every child to Love, Learn and Flourish together, guided by our values of Generosity, Friendship, Forgiveness, Hope, Trust and Courage.
We believe that school should be a place where children feel happy, safe, valued and inspired. We aim to make life at Woodchester as rich and varied as possible, providing a well-designed and engaging curriculum that gives every child the opportunity to discover their interests, recognise their strengths and develop a lifelong love of learning.
We want our children to understand that when we work together, there really are no limits to what we can achieve or the hopes we can have for the future. We encourage them to be curious, to ask questions, to embrace challenges and to have the courage to try new things.
We also know that our children are growing up in a rapidly changing world, where strength of character, kindness and resilience are more important than ever. Developing our school values is therefore central to everything we do. Whether it is showing generosity and friendship to others, finding forgiveness, having hope, building trust or showing courage, we look for opportunities to nurture these qualities throughout every aspect of school life.
At Woodchester, learning happens everywhere. It might be discovering the wonder of a dragonfly, getting lost in a new book, working together on a project, performing on stage, playing with friends or overcoming something that once seemed difficult. Each of these experiences helps our children to grow into confident, compassionate and well-rounded young people.
Our greatest hope is that every child leaves Woodchester with a smile on their face, wonderful memories of their primary school years, a strong sense of who they are and the skills, confidence and character they need to embrace whatever lies ahead.
We look forward to welcoming you to our Woodchester family.
Key Dates
We understand that parents are busy and try to ensure that we provide information upfront as much as we can throughout the school year. We hope that this calendar is useful as it contains key dates throughout the school year. If you have any questions, please contact the school office.
February 2023
We were inspected in February 2023 and were delighted with the outcome.
We are still an 'Outstanding' school!
Thank you to all our pupils, staff, governors, parents, and our church and local community for being such a fantastic team!
School Games Mark 24-25
We have achieved the School Games Gold Mark Award for the academic year 2024/25. This in recognition of our commitment to the development of competiton across our school and community. We are extremely proud of our pupils for their dedication to all aspects of school sport and physical activity. We look forward to applying once again in 2026!
February 2025
Our school is living up to its foundation as a Church school and is enabling pupils and adults to flourish. The school’s formidable commitment to a nurturing and inclusive environment results in pupils knowing their strengths.
STEM LEARNING SMALL SCHOOLS' HUB!
Our school has won an Enthuse grant of £25,000 from STEM York, a national organisation set up to improve young people’s lives through the power of STEM (Science, Technology and Maths). The Enthuse grant programme encourages schools to work in collaboration to improve the outcomes of pupils in STEM subjects so that they develop an understanding of the opportunities and careers that are available in STEM. This collaboration will allow us to build on the success of last year’s Primary Science Quality Mark and ensure that our children are well equipped to consider STEM careers of the future.

pageCache.text:
Our Vision - 2024
Our church school community seeks to inspire children and adults to love, learn and flourish together so we may become everything God has created us to be.
'Love, Learn and Flourish Together'
'Indeed, the body does not consist of one member but of many.' (1 Corinthians 12;14-16)
Our Christian vision is rooted in the desire to nurture our community - be it school, village, country or wider world - both now and in the future. It recognises that we are unique individuals, loved by God, each with our own strengths and talents to contribute and that by working together we can achieve more within our community and beyond.
The context of our vision
Our vision is based on 1 Corinthians 12: 14-16. The Apostle Paul wrote a letter to the Christians in Corinth responding to a letter they had sent to him asking for advice about worship and ethics. The heart of Paul’s answers in chapters 12-13 is that they should approach all the ethical dilemmas they faced and all the conflict they were experiencing in the knowledge that they were all members of the body of Christ and that they should behave towards each other with love.
1 Corinthians 12; 14-16
Just as a body, though one, has many parts, but all its many parts form one body, so it is with Christ. For we were all baptised by one Spirit so as to form one body – whether Jews or Gentiles, slave or free – and we were all given the one Spirit to drink. And so the body is not made up of one part but of many. (12-14)
Now if the foot should say, ‘Because I am not a hand, I do not belong to the body,’ it would not for that reason stop being part of the body. And if the ear should say, ‘Because I am not an eye, I do not belong to the body’, it would not for that reason stop being part of the body. If the whole body were an eye, where would the sense of hearing be? If the whole body were an ear, where would the sense of smell be. But in fact God has placed the parts on the body, every one of them, just as he wanted them to be. (15-18)
If they were all one part, where would the body be? As it is, that are many parts, but one body. (19)
What do we know about Paul?
Paul is probably the best known of all the early Christians. Before encountering Jesus on the road to Damascus he was a zealous Pharisee who sought to maintain the purity of Judaism. After his experience on the road to Damascus he turned to proclaiming Jesus among the Gentiles. He travelled around the Roman Empire proclaiming the good news of Jesus and founded communities of Christians as he went. He also wrote a large number of letters, 13 of which are preserved in the New Testament and 1 Corinthians is one of these.
July 2024 Review of Vision and Values
In July 2024, our community came together to review our school vision to see if it still fitted the aims of our school. We sought the views of Governors, Parents, Staff and Children and will be sending it out for review to the wider community in the autumn. We all agreed that our vision suited our school but that we wanted to simplify the values that were derived from our school vision and have agreed the following values and linked bible stories for our school:
Feeding of Five Thousand
Jesus quells the storm
Daniel and the Lion’s Den
In choosing our values we have considered the Christian festival calendar and linked bible stories so that children will better understand the value for the term and how it applies in their lives.
Vision and values day
We held a whole school vision and values day to allow our children to understand the basis of our school vision and its theological roots in 1 Corinthians. The day started with a whole school worship exploring the Bible verses that our vision is based on before moving to class activities based on love, learn and flourish together. Our school community created three wonderful pieces of whole school art which hang in our hall with pride.
